kp9:1.1: What should be done by one skilful in good,
kp9:1.2: who has comprehended the state of peace:
kp9:1.3: he ought to be able, straight, and upright, easy to speak to, meek, without conceit,
kp9:2.1: satisfied (with little), easy to support, free from duties, and light in living,
kp9:2.3: with faculties at peace, prudent, not forward, and greedless among the families,
kp9:3.1: he should not do the slightest thing whereby others who are wise might find fault (with him).
kp9:3.3: “(May all beings) be happy and secure,
kp9:3.4: may all beings in their hearts be happy!
kp9:4.1: Whatsoever breathing beings there are - trembling, firm, or any other (beings),
kp9:4.3: whether they be long or great, of middle size, short, tiny, or of compact (body),
kp9:5.1: those who are seen, and those who are unseen, those who live far away, those who are near,
kp9:5.3: those who are born, and those who still seek birth - may all beings in their hearts be happy!”
kp9:6.2: nor should he despise anyone wherever they be,
kp9:6.3: he should not long for suffering for another because of anger or resentment.
kp9:7.1: In the same way as a mother would protect her son, her only son, with her life,
kp9:7.3: so toward all beings he should develop the measureless thought (of friendliness).
kp9:7.4: Towards the whole wide world he should develop the measureless thought of friendliness,
kp9:8.3: above, below, and across (the middle), without barriers, hate, or enemy.
kp9:9.1: Standing, walking, sitting, lying, for as long as he is without torpor,
kp9:9.3: he should be resolved on this mindfulness, for this, they say here, is the (true) spiritual life.
kp9:10.1: Without going back to (wrong) views, virtuous, and endowed with (true) insight,
kp9:10.3: having removed (all) greed for sense pleasures,
kp9:10.4: he will never come to lie in a womb again.
